checks: The quantile polynomial increases strictly on (0,1) with endpoint values zero and one. Using the parent density and PL=dV gives exactly the threshold projection measure Pη^(d−1) and integrated volume b.

For any smaller projected measure, the signed-threshold inequality subtracts a strictly positive v0 times its missing measure and gives an integral strictly below b. The actual B sections have lengths bounded by the simplex lengths.
At b=V, Fubini gives equality of the two lengths almost everywhere, so the projection has full measure; the optimizer is T.

Chord-length concavity follows from Minkowski interpolation of interval sections, and the positive threshold projection is compact as the projection of T∩(T−v0e). Filling those entire chords thus gives a compact convex body with exactly b and the claimed projected measure.
The source 588e75e8ff86db2e §3 has the same actual convex attainment and no additional claim about sharpness of the roof bound.

dependencies.hypotheses: Use the exact same-wave chord distribution at d≥2 in the same direction, longitudinal coordinate and physical transverse measure. Its V, L, P and positive atomless chord law are precisely those used in the quantile integral. Predecessor review is required before admission.

overlap.comparison: Its sweep compares volume to the full t-span through a pointwise bound. It does not optimize the transverse projection of a subbody with prescribed volume.

readability: The positive threshold argument and the b=V boundary case are separated explicitly.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Selecting the largest chords gives the exact lower bound on transverse projection at a prescribed volume, and the optimizer is an actual convex subbody.
